newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh rebel leader says he expects peace.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh rebel leader says he expects peace.

text.p: A leader of tribal rebels fighting for autonomy in the Chittagong Hill Tracts region of Bangladesh expressed optimism on Saturday that a peace deal could be achieved with the government.
"We are hopeful for peace. Things are moving in a direction where we can expect a solution," Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma, chief of the political wing of the Shanti Bahini rebels, said.
"It's for peace why I am here," the soft-spoken Larma told reporters after a three-hour meeting in Dhaka with government negotiators.
It was the first time that Shanti Bahini had taken part in talks with the government outside the 5,500 sq mile (14,200 sq km) Hill Tracts region, which borders on India and Burma.

Earlier in the day, the five-member rebel team, led by Larma, flew to Dhaka aboard a military helicopter from Dudukchhari, a remote Hill Tracts village near the Indian border for talks aimed at ending the 23-year insurgency.
The government's chief negotiator, Abul Hasanat Abdullah, who is the parliamentary chief whip of the ruling Awami League, also spoke of "success" in Saturday's talks.
"We are heading towards a settlement. Both sides are sincere," Abdullah said.

Soon after taking office in June, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina formed a national committee, comprising representatives of the ruling and opposition parties, to boost intiatives to resolve the problems in the Hill Tracts.
Designated members of the committee from the largest opposition group, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) of former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia, did not take part.
Committee members said the talks would continue on Sunday.
In addition to automonmy, the Shanti Bahini (Peace Force) also wants 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.

Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which has forced around 50,000 tribespeople to seek refuge in the northeastern Indian state of Tripura.
